knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=The input single-cell expression matrix (e.g., data@assays$RNA@data) ;; sample=A vector indicating the sample of origin for each cell ;; celltype=A vector indicating the cell type for each cell ;; feature_types=The specific feature type to generate (e.g., "gene_mean_celltype") to save time ;; type=The type of single-cell data (e.g., "scrna") ;; ncores=Number of cores to use for parallel processing ;; species=The species of the dataset (e.g., "Homo sapiens") ;; scfeatures_result=The named list of feature dataframes used for reporting ;; output_folder=The directory path where the HTML report is saved
- alternatives: ClassifyR::crossValidate=Recommended for performing cross-validated classification on the generated features ;; survival and survminer=Used for downstream survival analysis and plotting Kaplan-Meier curves
- when_to_use: When you want to construct multi-view feature representations (sample x feature matrices) from single-cell or spatial transcriptomics data for downstream classification, survival analysis, or association studies.
- pitfalls: Running scFeatures with default parameters generates all feature types, which can be highly computationally intensive; specify a subset of feature_types to reduce run time ;; Downstream classification accuracy may be low if the input dataset is too small or lacks sufficient biological signal to distinguish conditions.

workflows.name: feature_generation_and_downstream_analysis
workflows.intent: Generate multi-view features from single-cell RNA-seq data and perform downstream classification or survival analysis.
input: metadata.csv (cell-level metadata containing sample and celltype annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Load single-cell expression and metadata ;; 2. Generate multi-view features using scFeatures ;; 3. Perform cross-validated classification using ClassifyR::crossValidate ;; 4. Perform hierarchical clustering and survival analysis using hclust and survival::survfit
workflows.code:
data("example_scrnaseq" , package = "scFeatures")
data <- example_scrnaseq

scfeatures_result <- scFeatures(data = data@assays$RNA@data, sample = data$sample, celltype = data$celltype,
                                feature_types = "gene_mean_celltype"  , 
                                type = "scrna",  
                                ncores = 1,  
                                species = "Homo sapiens")

feature_gene_mean_celltype <- scfeatures_result$gene_mean_celltype

# inspect the first 5 rows and first 5 columns
feature_gene_mean_celltype[1:5, 1:5]

# inspect the dimension of the matrix
dim(feature_gene_mean_celltype)

library(ClassifyR)

# X is the feature type generated
# y is the condition for classification
X <- feature_gene_mean_celltype
y <- data@meta.data[!duplicated(data$sample), ]
y <- y[match(rownames(X), y$sample), ]$condition

# run the classification model using random forest
result <- ClassifyR::crossValidate(
    X, y,
    classifier = "randomForest", nCores = 2,
    nFolds = 3, nRepeats = 5
)

ClassifyR::performancePlot(results = result)

library(survival)
library(survminer)
 

X <- feature_gene_mean_celltype
X <- t(X)

# run hierarchical clustering
hclust_res <- hclust(
    as.dist(1 - cor(X, method = "pearson")),
    method = "ward.D2"
)

set.seed(1)
# generate some survival outcome, including the survival days and the censoring outcome
survival_day <- sample(1:100, ncol(X))
censoring <- sample(0:1, ncol(X), replace = TRUE)

cluster_res <- cutree(hclust_res, k = 2)
metadata <- data.frame( cluster = factor(cluster_res),
                        survival_day = survival_day,
                        censoring = censoring)

# plot survival curve
fit <- survfit(
    Surv(survival_day, censoring) ~ cluster,
    data = metadata
)
ggsurv <- ggsurvplot(fit,
    conf.int = FALSE, risk.table = TRUE,
    risk.table.col = "strata", pval = TRUE
)
ggsurv

workflows.name: association_study_report
workflows.intent: Generate an HTML report visualizing the association of generated features with conditions.
input: scfeatures_result.rds (a named list of feature dataframes generated by scFeatures)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the generated scFeatures list ;; 2. Define the output directory ;; 3. Generate the HTML association study report using run_association_study_report
workflows.code:
# here we use the demo data from the package 
data("scfeatures_result" , package = "scFeatures")

# here we use the current working directory to save the html output
# modify this to save the html file to other directory
output_folder <-  tempdir()

run_association_study_report(scfeatures_result, output_folder )
